turns.belief_state: 逃避行为在短期内缓解了焦虑，但长期来看加重了无力感。

turns.speaker: therapist
turns.text: 感谢你的坦诚。长时间卧床和逃避，其实是我们在面对巨大压力时的自然自我保护防御机制。但它也会让我们的大脑不断沉浸在负性循环里。你觉不觉得，越是不去工作室，那些可怕的灾难化想象就越严重？
turns.belief_state: 行为回避维持了抑郁和焦虑的循环。

turns.speaker: client
turns.text: 确实是这样。我在家里脑子里就会乱想，甚至觉得连呼吸都困难。但我真的不知道去了工作室能做什么，那些账单还在那儿，我也拿不出钱来。
turns.belief_state: 面对现实问题感到能力不足，产生习得性无助。

turns.speaker: therapist
turns.text: 那我们今天能不能做一个小小的行为实验？不需要你立刻去解决所有债务问题，我们只设定一个非常小的目标：明天下午去工作室坐半个小时，只整理一下办公桌的图纸，不处理催款电话，看看会发生什么，你愿意尝试吗？
turns.belief_state: 通过行为激活和微小步骤打破回避循环，重建掌控感。

turns.speaker: client
turns.text: 半个小时……只整理图纸？这听起来好像没那么可怕，但我还是有点担心自己去了会情绪崩溃。
turns.belief_state: 客户对行为实验既有期待又伴随预期焦虑。

turns.speaker: therapist
turns.text: 崩溃了也没关系，那也是你真实情绪的流露。如果真的感到崩溃，你可以随时离开。我们可以把这看成一次探索，看看你的焦虑会不会像你想象的那样持续一整天，还是在达到某个峰值后会下降？
turns.belief_state: 帮助客户降低对负面情绪的灾难化恐惧，强调自主选择。

turns.speaker: client
turns.text: 好吧，那我试一试。周三下午我去半个小时，回来后向你汇报。另外，上周我们说到我不是个合格的父亲，我其实一直在想，我儿子看我的眼神好像并没有变，变的是我自己对自己的评判。
turns.emotional_state: 有所觉察、自我反思、平静
turns.belief_state: 核心信念开始受到挑战，客户开始主动审视自我批评的合理性。

sessions.ending_state: 完成了行为激活的初步设计，客户同意进行微型行为实验，并在认知层面自主反思了角色扮演的僵化信念。

sessions.goal: 回顾行为实验结果，重构核心信念，探讨弹性应对策略以巩固成效

turns.speaker: therapist
turns.text: 林伟，欢迎来。看你的气色比上周要放松一些，周三去工作室的实验顺利吗？
turns.belief_state: 关注行为实验的成效，强化积极的应对经验。

turns.speaker: client
turns.text: 挺有意思的。我周三去了，刚坐下时心跳确实很快，手心冒汗。但我强迫自己只看图纸，整理了大概二十分钟后，我发现那种窒息感竟然慢慢退下去了。而且我还順便给一个配合供应商发了邮件协商延期，对方居然答应了。
turns.belief_state: 事实证明灾难化预想并未发生，个人效能感有所恢复。

turns.speaker: therapist
turns.text: 太棒了！这说明什么？说明你的大脑虽然预测了灾难，但现实往往比想象的更有弹性。你在没有完全解决财务危机的情况下，通过一个微小的行动，重新夺回了一点掌控感。
turns.belief_state: 通过合作性经验主义验证了认知偏差，增强了自我效能。

turns.speaker: client
turns.text: 对，我发现自己并没有‘彻底完蛋’。虽然钱的问题还没完全解决，但我不是什么都做不好。我至少还能协商，还能设计，还能面对。
turns.belief_state: 我虽然遇到了困难，但并不代表我整个人失败了，犯错只是需要调整经营策略的信号。

turns.speaker: therapist
turns.text: 听到你这样总结，我非常高兴。回想我们第一次见面时，你觉得支票退回等于你整个人生的坍塌。现在，经过这几周的探索，你对这个事件和对自己的看法有什么新的理解吗？
turns.belief_state: 巩固认知重构成果，为未来的应变打下基础。

turns.speaker: client
turns.text: 我意识到以前我对自己太苛刻了。我总是把生意上的挫折当成我人格上的缺陷。其实创业本来就会有起伏，支票退回只是一个信号，提醒我需要调整财务流程和现金流管理，而不是判定我是一个不合格的丈夫、父亲和负责人。
turns.belief_state: 建立起更加灵活、客观和适应性的核心信念。

turns.speaker: therapist

turns.speaker: therapist

sessions.ending_state: Rupture successfully navigated; client acknowledged cognitive disconnect between evidence and emotional habit, though core belief remains firmly intact.

sessions.goal: Design and evaluate a small behavioral experiment to test the prediction that submitting work without excessive over-preparation leads to disaster.

turns.belief_state: 设计行为实验

turns.speaker: client
turns.text: 不行，这太危险了！如果他们觉得我销蝀了怎么劚？我不敢冒这个险。
turns.belief_state: 冒险等同于职业每亡

turns.speaker: therapist
turns.text: 我看到你的扛拒是那么真实。我们不急着做那么大的实验，我们可以先在一个不重要的小部分做个微实验，例如只将一个图标修改一遍就向同事展示。
turns.belief_state: 调整实验难度

turns.speaker: client
turns.text: 这样做……我还是会心怘。但毖定只是一个图标，我或许可以试一次。
turns.belief_state: 允许微小的极限测试

turns.speaker: therapist
turns.text: 好的，这就是我们的小实验。当你交出那个只修改一遍的图标时，我们来看看真实的响应是什么。
turns.belief_state: 聚焦实验目标

turns.speaker: client
turns.text: 其实我有点排斥你老是让我做实验，有时我觉得你不懂设计行业的压力。
turns.belief_state: 出现论治破裂

turns.speaker: therapist
turns.text: 谢谢你及时告诉我这个，这让我意识到我的笔调太促进了。我确实不懂设计，但我坚信你内心的慈悲可以比我们曵得更远。我们可以攲定更慢的节奏。
turns.belief_state: 修复论治破裂

sessions.ending_state: 基于为订正与认知破裂的修复，客户与治疗师达成了更加柔和的实验计划

sessions.goal: Establish collaborative empirical stance and identify automatic thoughts related to recent professional setbacks.

turns.speaker: therapist
turns.text: Hello Elena, thank you for coming today. How have you been since we set up this initial consultation?
turns.belief_state: Therapy is a collaborative journey.

turns.speaker: client
turns.text: Hello. I have been exhausted, honestly. Every time I open my laptop to update my portfolio, my chest gets tight and I just close it again.
turns.belief_state: I am incapable of fixing my career situation.

turns.speaker: therapist
turns.text: That chest tightness sounds really heavy. When that happens right before you open your laptop, what kinds of thoughts run through your mind?
turns.belief_state: Identifying specific automatic thoughts will help us test them together.

turns.speaker: client
turns.text: I think, 'What is the point? You sent out twenty applications and got nothing. You are clearly failing at the only thing you are supposed to be good at.'
turns.belief_state: My worth is entirely tied to professional output and job application results.

turns.speaker: therapist
turns.text: That is a very harsh absolute judgment. If we look at that thought as a hypothesis rather than an absolute fact, how might we test it?
turns.belief_state: Thoughts are hypotheses, not facts.

turns.speaker: client
turns.text: I do not know. It feels completely real when it happens. It does not feel like a hypothesis; it feels like the obvious truth.
turns.belief_state: My negative thoughts are undeniable facts.

turns.speaker: therapist
turns.text: It makes complete sense that it feels that way because you have practiced believing it for a long time. Would you be willing to examine the evidence together?
turns.belief_state: Collaborative empiricism requires client willingness and pacing.

turns.speaker: client
turns.text: I can try, but I am not sure what evidence there is other than the rejections in my inbox.
turns.belief_state: Willing to tentatively explore, though doubtful.

sessions.ending_state: Initial rapport established, introduction of the concept of treating thoughts as hypotheses with mild client hesitation.

sessions.goal: Examine intermediate beliefs and design a small behavioral experiment regarding portfolio work.

turns.speaker: therapist
turns.text: Welcome back, Elena. How was your week following our discussion about viewing thoughts as hypotheses?
turns.belief_state: Reviewing homework bridges sessions and tracks progress.

turns.speaker: client
turns.text: It was mixed. I tried to look at my portfolio on Thursday, but the thought 'If it is not flawless, it is a complete failure' popped up instantly and paralyzed me.
turns.belief_state: Perfectionism is the only acceptable standard.

turns.speaker: therapist
turns.text: That rule about perfection is powerful. Let us look at that underlying assumption: 'If it is not flawless, it is a complete failure.' Where do you think that rule came from?
turns.belief_state: Understanding origins of rules helps loosen their grip.

turns.speaker: client
turns.text: Probably from my upbringing. My parents always praised top grades, and anything less was met with silence. I learned that average means invisible.
turns.belief_state: My value depends entirely on achieving flawlessness.

turns.speaker: therapist
turns.text: That is a heavy burden to carry for thirty-four years. Would you be open to running a behavioral experiment this week to test what happens if you intentionally produce something imperfect?
turns.belief_state: Behavioral experiments provide experiential data against rigid beliefs.

turns.speaker: client
turns.text: Honestly, that sounds terrifying. If I submit an imperfect design, people will think I am incompetent. That feels risky.
turns.belief_state: Imperfect work will result in immediate social and professional rejection.

turns.speaker: therapist
turns.text: We do not have to submit it publicly. What if we just design a low-stakes sketch where you intentionally leave one element unfinished and notice your anxiety levels?
turns.belief_state: Graduated exposure reduces anxiety and fosters compliance.

turns.speaker: client
turns.text: Okay, a private sketch where I leave something unfinished. I think I can manage that without panicking too much.
turns.belief_state: A controlled, low-stakes experiment feels approachable.

sessions.ending_state: Agreed on a low-stakes behavioral experiment involving an intentionally imperfect private sketch.

sessions.goal: Review the behavioral experiment, address a therapeutic rupture regarding perceived pressure, and refine cognitive restructuring.

turns.speaker: therapist
turns.text: Hello Elena. How did the private sketch experiment go this week?
turns.belief_state: Reviewing experiments provides empirical data for cognitive shifts.

turns.speaker: client
turns.text: I actually did not do it. I felt so much pressure leading up to it that I avoided my desk entirely. I felt like you were disappointed in me before I even started.
turns.belief_state: I have let my therapist down and cannot meet expectations.

turns.speaker: therapist
turns.text: I appreciate you telling me that directly. It sounds like there was a rupture and you felt judged or pressured by me. Can we unpack what happened?
turns.belief_state: Addressing ruptures transparently strengthens the therapeutic alliance.

turns.speaker: client
turns.text: I just felt like my old perfectionism had sneaked right into therapy. I had to perform the experiment correctly, which defeated the whole purpose.
turns.belief_state: I turned therapy into another test I could fail.

turns.speaker: therapist
turns.text: That is a profound insight, Elena. You turned the homework into another test. There is no failing here. What does it tell you that even self-care felt like a test?
turns.belief_state: Recognizing core patterns in session dynamics deepens awareness.

turns.speaker: client
turns.text: It tells me that my inner critic is running the show, even when I am trying to heal. It exhausts me.
turns.belief_state: The inner critic pervades every aspect of my life.

turns.speaker: therapist
turns.text: It is exhausting. Knowing this now, how can we design something for next week that removes any hint of a 'pass or fail' grading system?
turns.belief_state: Adjusting the intervention to bypass the performance trap is essential.

turns.speaker: client
turns.text: Maybe just scribbling with my non-dominant hand for five minutes with no goal at all. Just pure mess.
turns.belief_state: True play and experimentation require total absence of performance metrics.

sessions.ending_state: Successfully navigated a rupture regarding performance pressure and collaboratively redesigned the upcoming experiment.

sessions.goal: 建立协作关系，收集近期社交焦虑情境的负面自动思维，初步引入认知行为框架。

turns.speaker: therapist
turns.text: 林晓你好，欢迎来到咨询室。我们今天可以先聊聊近期最困扰你的社交情况，看看你想从哪里开始？
turns.belief_state: 咨询师相信通过协作能帮助来访者理清思绪。

turns.speaker: client
turns.text: 你好。其实我一直很犹豫要不要来，因为我觉得我的问题可能挺可笑的。就是每次在公司开会或者和大家一起吃饭，我都觉得大家在盯着我，觉得我很无能。
turns.belief_state: 如果我在别人面前表现出紧张，他们就会看不起我。

turns.speaker: therapist
turns.text: 听到你这么说，能感觉到这带给你不少压力。你提到觉得大家在盯着你、觉得你无能，这让你在现场非常难受吧？能具体说说最近一次发生这种情况的情景吗？
turns.belief_state: 倾听具体情境有助于识别核心的自动思维。

turns.speaker: client
turns.text: 上周部门例会上，主管让我简短汇报一下新项目的平面排版。我一开口声音就在抖，我觉得我当时结巴了。我脑子里马上下了一个结论：完蛋了，所有人都在心里笑话我，觉得我连基本的话都说不好。
turns.belief_state: 我的紧张情绪太明显了，别人一定在嘲笑我的软弱。

turns.speaker: therapist
turns.text: 这是一个非常典型的灾难化预测。当你说完“完蛋了，所有人都觉得我连基本的话都说不好”时，这种想法就像是一个绝对真理一样压在你心头。我们可以把它记录下来，作为我们后续一起检验的假设，而不是绝对的事实，你觉得呢？
turns.belief_state: 自动思维可以被识别并作为检验的对象。

turns.speaker: client
turns.text: 理性上我知道可能没那么夸张，但当时那种感觉太真实了。我甚至觉得主管后来看我的那一眼就是在嫌弃我。我没办法控制自己不去这么想。
turns.belief_state: 虽然理智上知道不一定全是真的，但我无法停止这种灾难化联想。

turns.speaker: therapist
turns.text: 这种“无法控制”的感觉常常让我们更急于逃避。不过，我们今天不需要立刻改变它，只需要把它当成一个研究课题。你看，我们能不能把刚才的想法写下来，看看它包含了哪些证据和反证？
turns.belief_state: 协作性经验主义能帮助来访者与自身思维保持距离。

turns.speaker: client
turns.text: 好吧，如果只是像做实验那样看看的话，我倒是觉得没那么大压力。写下来也许能让我看得更清楚一点。
turns.belief_state: 将思维外化能减轻即时的情感负荷。

sessions.ending_state: 来访者初步理解了认知行为治疗中“想法不等于事实”的概念，并同意将特定社交情境中的自动思维进行记录和观察。

sessions.goal: 审视思维记录单，探讨灾难化预测与中间信念，识别“读心术”认知谬误。

turns.speaker: therapist
turns.text: 林晓，这周过得怎么样？上周我们布置了一个小任务，尝试记录几个社交时的自动思维，你带来了吗？
turns.belief_state: 查看家庭作业能了解来访者一周的认知加工情况。

turns.speaker: client
turns.text: 带来了。我记了两条。周三午休时，同事们围在一起聊天，我走过去的时候他们正好停顿了一下，我立刻就想：他们肯定在讨论我刚才设计方案里的漏洞，觉得我很笨。结果我端着咖啡又默默走开了。
turns.belief_state: 别人安静下来一定是在背后议论我。

turns.speaker: therapist
turns.text: 这是一个很好的例子。你看，当同事停顿的时候，你的脑子里迅速出现了一个结论：“他们在讨论我的漏洞，觉得我很笨”。在CBT里，这被称为“读心术”，也就是我们在没有确凿证据的情况下，假设自己知道别人在想什么。你觉得，除了这个解释外，还可能有哪些其他原因呢？
turns.belief_state: 识别认知谬误有助于拓宽解释视角。

turns.speaker: client
turns.text: （沉默了几秒）可能……他们只是刚好聊完了一个话题？或者在商量中午点什么外卖？但我很难相信这些别的可能，因为我总觉得只要我在场，别人就应该把注意力放在我身上或者审视我。
turns.belief_state: 我是所有人关注的焦点，任何风吹草动都与我有关。

turns.speaker: therapist
turns.text: 你刚才提到“只要我在场，别人就应该审视我”，这句话里藏着一个挺重的标准。这种认为自己必须完美、或者时刻受到审视的信念，是从哪里来的呢？
turns.belief_state: 表面思维背后往往连结着更深层的核心或中间信念。

turns.speaker: client
turns.text: 我父母从小就对我的成绩要求很高。我记得初中时有一次考试退步了名次，我爸妈虽然没打我，但那种失望的眼神让我觉得，我如果表现不好，就是个失败者，不值得被认可。我是不是有点把对他们的恐惧转移到同事身上了？
turns.belief_state: 如果我不能持续保持高水平的表现，我就是个彻头彻尾的失败者。

turns.speaker: therapist
turns.text: 你很有觉察力，能够看到过去的经历和现在的感受之间的桥梁。那些早期的期许变成了你心里的一根鞭子，让你对任何微小的“失误”都如临大敌。今天我们先走到这里，看到这个核心规则，对你来说有什么感觉？
turns.belief_state: 来访者展现出良好的自我反思与整合能力。

turns.speaker: client
turns.text: 感觉挺沉重的，但也有一种终于找到源头的感觉。原来不是我真的那么差，而是我心里那套评判标准太苛刻了。
turns.belief_state: 苛刻的评判标准是导致焦虑的根源，而非自身无能。

sessions.ending_state: 成功连接了早期家庭经验与当前社交焦虑中的严苛核心信念，来访者体验到情感上的释然与些许疲惫。

sessions.goal: 设计并评估小型行为实验，检验“如果我在别人面前表现出紧张，他们就会嫌弃我”这一假设。

turns.speaker: therapist
turns.text: 林晓，上周我们探讨了你对自己的高标准和“读心术”倾向。这周你想把这些讨论转化为一个什么样的实际行动，来检验一下我们的假设呢？
turns.belief_state: 行为实验是CBT核心干预手段，必须由来访者自主设计。

turns.speaker: client
turns.text: 其实我有点抗拒。你上周说要做行为实验，我一想到要在开会时故意表现得很紧张或者说错话，我就浑身不舒服。我觉得这太冒险了，万一真的像我想的那样，大家翻白眼怎么办？
turns.belief_state: 行为实验风险太高，无法承受失败后果。

turns.speaker: therapist
turns.text: 我完全理解你的顾虑。这是一个小小的危机或叫“卡点”，我们不需要强迫自己去做任何超出舒适区太多的事。我们可以把实验设计得非常安全，比如从小幅度的尝试开始。你觉得有什么是你可以掌控的？
turns.belief_state: 尊重来访者的节奏，处理治疗中的微小阻抗。

turns.speaker: client
turns.text: 嗯……如果只是在日常沟通里，比如跟信任的同事说话时，不小心承认自己有点紧张，或者在发言时语速稍微放慢、允许自己卡壳两秒，这或许是我还能勉强接受的。
turns.belief_state: 可控范围内的微小暴露是可行的。

turns.speaker: therapist
turns.text: 这听起来是一个非常聪明的折中方案。既保留了你的控制感，又触碰到了你的核心恐惧。那我们来预测一下：如果这样做，最坏的结果是什么？发生的概率有多大？
turns.belief_state: 通过预测和概率计算来降低灾难化预期。

turns.speaker: client
turns.text: 最坏的结果是对方会觉得我很无能，概率大概有百分之五十吧。但我内心深处其实也知道，平时别人如果对我说他们紧张，我并不会笑话他们，反而会觉得挺自然的。
turns.belief_state: 双重标准正在被打破，同理心开始向自身延伸。

turns.speaker: therapist
turns.text: 这是一个非常宝贵的发现。你对自己和对别人往往采用着两套不同的标准。我们把这个实验记录下来，本周尝试一到两次，看看现实是否真的如你预测的那样糟糕，好吗？
turns.belief_state: 双重标准的识别有助于重塑核心信念。

turns.speaker: client
turns.text: 好的，我愿意试试。虽然还是有点心慌，但比起完全逃避，我觉得这个办法更踏实一些。
turns.belief_state: 愿意承担可控风险，展现出积极的疗效动能。

sessions.ending_state: 成功处理了来访者对行为实验的阻抗，通过协商制定了微型暴露实验计划，来访者表现出良好的自主意愿。

sessions.goal: Establish collaborative empiricism and map out the cycle between bodily sensations and catastrophic thoughts.

turns.speaker: therapist
turns.text: Hello Julian. It is good to meet you. As we begin, I want to make sure we work together as a team to understand what brings you in today and what you would like to explore.
turns.belief_state: Collaborative rapport is essential for effective cognitive restructuring.

turns.speaker: client
turns.text: Thanks for seeing me. I am here because my body feels like it is constantly working against me. Every time my heart beats a bit faster, I assume something is fundamentally wrong, like a heart attack.
turns.belief_state: Any sudden spike in my heart rate means my body is about to fail me.

turns.speaker: therapist
turns.text: That sounds exhausting to live with. When you notice that rapid heartbeat, what thoughts immediately run through your mind?
turns.belief_state: Identifying automatic thoughts will help reveal the cognitive link to physical sensations.

turns.speaker: client
turns.text: I immediately think I am going to collapse right there, and that everyone will stare at me and judge me. I cannot bear the thought of losing control in public.
turns.belief_state: If I lose control of my breathing in public, people will judge me and I will not survive the embarrassment.

turns.speaker: therapist
turns.text: So there is a powerful prediction that physical arousal equals public catastrophe. Let us write this down and examine it together as a hypothesis rather than an absolute fact.
turns.belief_state: Treating thoughts as hypotheses reduces their immediate threat value.

turns.speaker: client
turns.text: I suppose we can look at it that way, though it feels very real when it happens. Sometimes I wonder if it is just anxiety, but I cannot be sure.
turns.belief_state: Perhaps these physical sensations are just normal anxiety responses, though I cannot be entirely certain.

turns.speaker: therapist
turns.text: It is completely understandable that you feel uncertain. For our first experiment between now and next time, would you be willing to simply track when these sensations arise without trying to stop them immediately?
turns.belief_state: Observational monitoring builds self-awareness without overwhelming the client.

turns.speaker: client
turns.text: I can try tracking them, though just thinking about paying attention to my heart makes it race a little right now.
turns.belief_state: Monitoring physical symptoms might trigger the very anxiety I want to avoid.

sessions.ending_state: Session concluded with a collaborative agreement to track somatic triggers, though Julian remains mildly apprehensive about focusing on his heart rate.

sessions.goal: Review thought logs and explore behavioral experiments regarding physiological arousal.

turns.speaker: therapist
turns.text: Welcome back, Julian. How did the tracking go over the past week? What did you notice when those physical sensations popped up?
turns.belief_state: Reviewing self-monitoring data provides concrete material for cognitive work.

turns.speaker: client
turns.text: I did some tracking, but honestly, I felt like you were asking me to stare directly into a fire. When my heart rate went up on Tuesday, I just avoided leaving my desk entirely.
turns.belief_state: Avoiding physical triggers is the only way to keep myself safe from catastrophe.

turns.speaker: therapist
turns.text: I hear you, and I appreciate your honesty. It sounds like tracking felt more like a demand than a collaborative experiment, and that my suggestion pushed you into avoidance. Am I understanding that correctly?
turns.belief_state: Addressing ruptures early preserves the therapeutic alliance.

turns.speaker: client
turns.text: Yes, exactly. It felt like homework from school where I was bound to fail. I do not want to force myself into a panic attack.
turns.belief_state: The therapist is listening and is not trying to force me into danger.

turns.speaker: therapist
turns.text: Thank you for telling me that. We control the pace completely. If behavioral experiments feel too large right now, what is a tiny, safe way we could test your prediction about your heart?
turns.belief_state: Client agency is paramount in pacing exposure and experiments.

turns.speaker: client
turns.text: Maybe walking briskly up a flight of stairs on purpose? That makes my heart beat fast, but I am in a familiar building.
turns.belief_state: I can choose a controlled way to experience elevated heart rate without danger.

turns.speaker: therapist
turns.text: That is a brilliant, self-directed experiment. What prediction would we be testing if you walked up those stairs?
turns.belief_state: Linking deliberate actions to explicit predictions clarifies cognitive distortions.

turns.speaker: client
turns.text: The prediction is that my heart rate will spike, but that my body will actually handle it and settle down on its own without a medical emergency.
turns.belief_state: A rapid heartbeat from exertion might be different from a spontaneous panic attack.

sessions.ending_state: Rupture successfully navigated through collaborative pacing; Julian designed his own behavioral experiment involving stairs.

sessions.goal: Evaluate the outcome of the stair experiment and update core cognitive formulations.

turns.speaker: therapist
turns.text: Julian, how did your experiment go this week with walking up the stairs?
turns.belief_state: Reviewing behavioral experiments consolidates new learning.

turns.speaker: client
turns.text: I actually did it twice. The first time, my heart raced and I panicked a bit. The second time, I noticed my heart raced just as much, but nothing bad happened. I just breathed through it.
turns.belief_state: Physical arousal from exertion does not automatically lead to catastrophic failure.

turns.speaker: therapist
turns.text: That is a profound observation. What does that tell you about the relationship between a fast heartbeat and catastrophe?
turns.belief_state: Guided discovery helps the client generate their own cognitive shifts.

turns.speaker: client
turns.text: It tells me that my body knows how to regulate itself, and that a fast heart rate is just... well, a fast heart rate. It is not necessarily an alarm bell.
turns.belief_state: My body is resilient and capable of handling normal physiological fluctuations.

turns.speaker: therapist
turns.text: How does holding that new perspective feel in your body right now as we talk about it?
turns.belief_state: Integrating cognitive shifts with somatic awareness deepens therapy outcomes.

turns.speaker: client
turns.text: It feels lighter. My shoulders are less tense. Though I still worry about crowded places where I cannot easily escape if I do feel dizzy.
turns.belief_state: Progress has been made, but secondary avoidance behaviors remain unaddressed.

turns.speaker: therapist
turns.text: That makes total sense. We have tackled the internal heart rate fear, but crowds are a different domain. We can take our time looking at that whenever you feel ready.
turns.belief_state: Remaining pacing-oriented prevents overwhelming the client with unresolved material.

turns.speaker: client
turns.text: I appreciate that. I think I want to work on the crowd issue next, but I am glad we built this foundation first.
turns.belief_state: Collaborative therapy gives me the confidence to face remaining challenges.

sessions.ending_state: Session ended with successful integration of the stair experiment, acknowledging remaining work around public venues for future sessions.

sessions.goal: 建立咨询同盟，评估近期财务危机带来的情绪反应并识别初始自动思维。

turns.speaker: therapist
turns.text: 林伟你好，欢迎来到咨询室。最近这段时间过得怎么样？今天有什么特别想聊聊的吗？
turns.belief_state: 建立安全、合作的氛围

turns.speaker: client
turns.text: 谢谢。其实这一周过得很煎熬，可以说是焦头烂额。工作室的客户支票接连退票，我感觉自己快要撑不下去了。
turns.belief_state: 我正处于巨大的危机之中，没人能帮我

turns.speaker: therapist
turns.text: 听到支票接连退票，这对你和工作室来说确实是一个非常巨大的打击和压力源。当这些事情发生时，你脑海里最先跳出来的是什么样的想法？
turns.belief_state: 引导客户关注事件触发的自动思维

turns.speaker: client
turns.text: 脑子里一直有个声音在说：‘我是一个彻底的失败者，连基本的家庭开销都无法保障。’我觉得自己太没用了。
turns.belief_state: 我是一个彻底的失败者，无法保障家庭

turns.speaker: therapist
turns.text: ‘我是一个彻底的失败者，无法保障家庭。’这是一个非常沉重的想法，林伟。当我们对自己下这样的结论时，它往往会带来巨大的痛苦。你觉得这个想法在多大程度上是真实的呢？
turns.belief_state: 帮助客户客观审视负面自动思维

turns.speaker: client
turns.text: 理智上我知道也许不是全部，但情绪上我完全没办法反驳。事实就摆在眼前，账上的数字就是零，我就是没赚到钱。
turns.belief_state: 现实的财务结果直接等于我个人的全部价值

turns.speaker: therapist
turns.text: 账面现金流的短缺是一个真实的商业困难，这我们不否认。但我们可以把‘商业经营遇到挫折’和‘我是一个彻底的失败者’这两个概念暂时分离开来看看吗？看看它们是不是完全是一回事。
turns.belief_state: 区分事实与过度泛化的自我评价

turns.speaker: client
turns.text: 分开？对我来说挺难的。从小到大，家里人都认为成败由结果决定。不过……也许我的设计作品本身并不差，只是这次收款环节出了问题？
turns.belief_state: 我的专业能力或许没有完全失效，但挫折感依然存在

sessions.ending_state: 建立了初步的合作同盟，识别出了核心的自动思维，客户开始尝试将商业困境与自我价值做初步的分离，但内心仍感沉重。

sessions.goal: 审查上周的认知记录表，探讨“他人会看不起我”的中间信念。

turns.speaker: therapist
turns.text: 林伟，过去这一周过得怎么样？有尝试记录下那些让你感到特别焦虑的时刻吗？
turns.belief_state: 复盘家庭作业，推进CBT结构化流程

turns.speaker: client
turns.text: 我有记录。最难受的一次是周三，同行朋友约我喝咖啡，我满脑子都在想‘如果他知道我连员工工资都快发不出了，他肯定会看不起我，甚至在背后笑话我’，所以我最后找借口推脱了。
turns.belief_state: 如果别人知道我的财务困境，他们一定会看不起我

turns.speaker: therapist
turns.text: 你选择逃避那个聚会，因为你预判了别人的反应，这让你感到了强烈的羞耻和保护自己的冲动。我们来看看，这个‘别人一定会看不起我’的想法，证据是什么呢？
turns.belief_state: 引导客户搜集支持与反对该信念的证据

turns.speaker: client
turns.text: 证据？我以前听过他评价别人公司倒闭时说的话，语气挺严厉的。我觉得换作我，他也会那样看我。
turns.belief_state: 过去的零星言论可以证明他人的绝对苛刻

turns.speaker: therapist
turns.text: 所以你根据他过去对别人的评价，推导出了他也会这样对待陷入困境的你。这里面是不是有一种‘读心术’的成分？我们能不能设计一个小小的行为实验来检验一下这个想法，而不是只靠猜测？
turns.belief_state: 识别认知谬误，引入行为实验

turns.speaker: client
turns.text: 行为实验？你是让我去告诉他我破产了？这绝对不行，我做不到，这太丢脸了！我甚至觉得你根本不懂这种家庭和圈子里的面子有多重要。
turns.belief_state: 咨询师不理解我的处境，要求我做极其危险的事

turns.speaker: therapist
turns.text: 我听到你现在非常抗拒，甚至觉得我没有真正体会到面子对你的重要性。我很抱歉刚才的提议让你感到被推到了风口浪尖上。我们完全不需要向任何人直接坦白全部隐私，实验可以是非常温和、安全的。你愿意听听我的想法，或者我们一起调整方案吗？
turns.belief_state: 处理咨询过程中的 ruptures，重建协作

turns.speaker: client
turns.text: ……好吧，我刚才情绪有点激动。我只是太害怕暴露出去了。如果不是直接说财务状况，还能做什么实验？
turns.belief_state: 愿意重新听取调整后的温和方案

sessions.ending_state: 处理了一次关于干预过快的咨询师-客户误解（rupture），调整了干预策略，客户情绪由防御转为愿意继续探讨安全实验。

sessions.goal: 设计并评估温和的行为实验，探讨中间信念与过往家庭期待的关联。

turns.speaker: therapist
turns.text: 林伟，上周我们讨论后，你对那个‘行为实验’有什么新的想法或者担忧吗？
turns.belief_state: 尊重客户节奏，回顾上周进展

turns.speaker: client
turns.text: 后来我想了想，觉得上周是我反应过激了。不过我还是不想对朋友说实话。上周我试着跟妻子稍微透露了部分现金流的压力，结果她并没有我想象的那么崩溃，反而安慰我说可以一起精简开销。
turns.belief_state: 伴侣并没有我想象的那么苛刻，沟通并非绝路

turns.speaker: therapist
turns.text: 这是一个非常棒的发现！你原本以为把压力说出来会引发灾难，但实际上妻子的反应是支持和接纳的。这打破了你的一些悲观预设。你觉得这个经历对你有什么启发？
turns.belief_state: 通过真实数据巩固认知转变

turns.speaker: client
turns.text: 说明我可能总是把周围人想象得跟我的大家庭一样严厉。我爸妈以前对我和哥哥要求极高，稍微亏钱就觉得是奇耻大辱。我好像把这种老旧的标准套在了所有人身上。
turns.belief_state: 我的苛刻标准来源于家庭期待而非客观现实

turns.speaker: therapist
turns.text: 你敏锐地察觉到了核心信念的源头——来自原生家庭对成就和经济独立的极高期待。这不仅让你背负了公司的成败，还背负了沉重的道德审判。我们接下来可以看看，这个旧地图现在还适合用来导航你的人生吗？
turns.belief_state: 连接核心信念与过往经历，探讨其适应不良性

turns.speaker: client
turns.text: 不适合了。我已经38岁了，我有自己的家庭和妻子，不需要再用我爸的那套尺子来量自己的价值。虽然工作室的钱还没全追回来，但至少我知道自己不是孤立无援的。
turns.belief_state: 开始构建新的核心信念：我可以面对困难，且我的价值不全由金钱决定

turns.speaker: therapist
turns.text: 听到你这样说我很高兴。你不仅看清了枷锁，还在主动松绑。接下来的日子里，我们可以继续制定一个具体的应对方案，把注意力从‘证明自己不失败’转移到‘解决具体的经营问题’上来。
turns.belief_state: 巩固治疗成效，制定下一步行动计划

turns.speaker: client
turns.text: 好，我觉得这个方向很实用。下午我打算先去和律师谈谈追索支票的法律途径，不再光坐在办公室里胡思乱想了。
turns.belief_state: 从反刍思维转向建设性行动

sessions.ending_state: 客户成功完成了非正式行为实验（与妻子沟通），识别出核心信念源自原生家庭，焦虑显著下降，主动转向建设性的应对行动，治疗取得实质性进展。

sessions.goal: Establish collaborative empirical framework and explore the core belief about fundamental incompetence regarding graphic design tasks.

turns.speaker: therapist
turns.text: Hello Elena, thank you for coming in today. How have things been since we initially set up this consultation?
turns.belief_state: Establishing collaborative alliance

turns.speaker: client
turns.text: Honestly, I have been feeling quite anxious. I spent the entire weekend staring at a new brand layout assignment, convinced I am going to mess it up completely.
turns.belief_state: I am fundamentally incompetent and unable to handle complex tasks independently.

turns.speaker: therapist
turns.text: That heavy sense of dread sounds exhausting. When you looked at the layout, what specific thoughts went through your mind about your capability?
turns.belief_state: Exploring automatic thoughts linked to competence

turns.speaker: client
turns.text: I thought that real designers just know what to do instantly, and the fact that I had to sketch three different drafts means I am just faking it.
turns.belief_state: If I make a single mistake, it proves that I do not belong in my career field.

turns.speaker: therapist
turns.text: That is a very demanding standard. Notice how you are defining 'real designers' as never needing multiple drafts. Would you be open to examining whether that rule holds true for others?
turns.belief_state: Introducing collaborative empiricism

turns.speaker: client
turns.text: I guess senior designers sketch out ideas too, but for me, it feels different. For me, it feels like proof of my inadequacy.
turns.belief_state: My errors are uniquely damning to me.

turns.speaker: therapist
turns.text: It seems there is a double standard between how you view your own creative process versus others. How does it feel to label that distinction right now?
turns.belief_state: Highlighting cognitive asymmetry

turns.speaker: client
turns.text: It feels a bit uncomfortable, almost like you are minimizing how hard things are for me. Maybe my struggles really are just worse than everyone else's.
turns.belief_state: Rupture: feeling dismissed by therapist

turns.speaker: therapist
turns.text: I am glad you told me that. I certainly did not mean to minimize your very real distress. Let us pause on that; it sounds like my pushing for the double standard felt dismissive of your pain.
turns.belief_state: Repairing therapeutic alliance

turns.speaker: client
turns.text: Yeah, it did a bit. But I appreciate you checking. I just feel so tired of fighting my own brain every single day.
turns.belief_state: Softening defense

sessions.ending_state: Session concluded with a repaired alliance after a minor rupture regarding the pace of cognitive challenging, leaving the core belief unexamined for now but building trust.

sessions.goal: Examine the origin of the rule regarding luck versus skill in achievements, building on last week's repair.

turns.speaker: therapist
turns.text: Welcome back, Elena. How has your week been since our last conversation about how difficult it is to challenge those internal standards?
turns.belief_state: Continuity from previous session

turns.speaker: client
turns.text: It was up and down. I actually finished the brand layout and my supervisor said it was good, but my immediate thought was that she was just being polite.
turns.belief_state: My successes are merely the result of luck rather than my actual skill.

turns.speaker: therapist
turns.text: Ah, discounting the positive. When your supervisor praised the work, how did you quickly convert that data into 'just being polite'?
turns.belief_state: Examining cognitive filters

turns.speaker: client
turns.text: Because I know how many flaws were hidden in those vectors. If she had looked closer, she would have hated it. So her praise cannot be real.
turns.belief_state: If there are flaws, the whole product is worthless.

turns.speaker: therapist
turns.text: Let us design a behavioral experiment for this coming week. What if you explicitly asked your supervisor for one piece of specific constructive feedback on an element you felt unsure about?
turns.belief_state: Proposing empirical test

turns.speaker: client
turns.text: Ask her directly about my flaws? That sounds terrifying. What if she confirms that my work is terrible?
turns.belief_state: Asking for feedback invites catastrophe.

turns.speaker: therapist
turns.text: It is definitely a bold step. We don't have to do it if it feels too overwhelming right now, but it would give us concrete evidence instead of relying on mind-reading.
turns.belief_state: Respecting client agency

turns.speaker: client
turns.text: Let me think about it. Maybe I can ask a trusted peer instead of the supervisor first, just to test the waters.
turns.belief_state: Modifying experiment for safety

turns.speaker: therapist
turns.text: Starting with a trusted peer is a wonderful modification. You are designing the experiment yourself.
turns.belief_state: Reinforcing client autonomy

sessions.ending_state: Session ended with a collaboratively modified behavioral experiment to test assumptions about work quality with a peer.

sessions.goal: Review the peer feedback experiment, address avoidance patterns, and evaluate the belief about catastrophic consequences of mistakes.

turns.speaker: therapist
turns.text: How did your modified experiment go with your peer this week, Elena?
turns.belief_state: Checking on behavioral homework

turns.speaker: client
turns.text: Well... I chickened out. I wrote the message to my coworker, but I deleted it before sending because I thought, 'Why bother them with my insecurities?'
turns.belief_state: I am too weak to follow through.

turns.speaker: therapist
turns.text: Notice that quick shift to self-criticism. You didn't do the experiment, and immediately you conclude you are weak. What if we look at the avoidance itself as understandable information?
turns.belief_state: Reframing avoidance as protection

turns.speaker: client
turns.text: It feels like failure, plain and simple. Every time I plan to do something brave and back out, it proves I am stuck.
turns.belief_state: All-or-nothing thinking about progress

turns.speaker: therapist
turns.text: If a friend told you they backed out of a scary conversation, would you call them a failure, or would you recognize how high the anxiety was?
turns.belief_state: Encouraging perspective shift

turns.speaker: client
turns.text: I would tell them to take a breath and try again later. But for me, it is different because I am supposed to be past this by now.
turns.belief_state: Maintaining double standard for self

turns.speaker: therapist
turns.text: That 'supposed to' rule carries a lot of weight. Where do you think that rule comes from, expecting yourself to heal or grow without any setbacks?
turns.belief_state: Exploring conditional assumptions

turns.speaker: client
turns.text: Probably from my family background. In my house, mistakes were things to be corrected instantly, not analyzed or felt. If you struggled, you just weren't trying hard enough.
turns.belief_state: Tracing core belief origins

turns.speaker: therapist
turns.text: That makes total sense of why setbacks feel so dangerous to you. You were taught that struggle equals moral failing.
turns.belief_state: Synthesizing developmental context

turns.speaker: client
turns.text: Yeah. It is hard to break out of that, even when I know intellectually that it is harsh.
turns.belief_state: Unresolved tension between intellectual and emotional belief

sessions.ending_state: Session concluded with valuable insight into family origins of perfectionism, though the client remains caught between intellectual understanding and emotional self-blame regarding the failed homework.

sessions.goal: 建立咨询同盟并识别来访者近期失落感背后的核心自动化思维。

turns.speaker: therapist
turns.text: 晓晴你好，欢迎来到咨询室。最近这段时间，你觉得最困扰你的是什么呢？
turns.belief_state: 咨询师处于开放和支持的状态

turns.speaker: client
turns.text: 老师，我最近真的很累，每天去上课都觉得喘不过气。上学期期末成绩出来后，我发现自己居然只是中游，这在以前是不可想象的。
turns.belief_state: 成绩下降意味着我失去了原有的价值

turns.speaker: therapist
turns.text: 听到你从一个对自我要求很高的优秀学生，到现在面对成绩中游的落差，那种冲击一定很难受。当你看向那个成绩时，脑海里冒出的第一个想法是什么？
turns.belief_state: 需要引导来访者关注当下的自动化思维

turns.speaker: client
turns.text: 我脑子里一直有个声音在说：‘你真是一个失败者，你什么都做不对，以后肯定也找不到工作，父母也会对你失望透顶。’
turns.belief_state: 我是一个失败者，我将永远不会幸福

turns.speaker: therapist
turns.text: 这是一个非常沉重的标签——‘失败者’。每当你对自己说这句话时，它带给你的情绪和身体反应是什么样的呢？
turns.belief_state: 认知与情绪之间存在明确的连结

turns.speaker: client
turns.text: 我就更不想去上课了，只想缩在宿舍里睡觉。我觉得反正努力也没用，结果都一样糟糕。
turns.belief_state: 努力也无济于事，回避能带来短暂的安全感

turns.speaker: therapist
turns.text: 这听起来像是一个恶性循环：消极的评价引发了无助感，而无助感让你选择了回避，进而让你失去了改变现状的机会。我们能不能试着把这个思维记录下来，看看它是不是绝对的真理？
turns.belief_state: 思维不是事实，可以通过协作进行检验

turns.speaker: client
turns.text: 或许吧，但我现在觉得这些想法很难改变，它们就像真的一样。
turns.belief_state: 旧有的认知根深蒂固，改变极其困难

sessions.ending_state: 初步建立了咨询同盟，识别出了核心的自动化思维和行为回避模式，但来访者对改变持保留态度。

sessions.goal: 引入行为激活策略，并探讨上节课布置的思维记录作业所遇到的阻抗与误解。

turns.speaker: therapist
turns.text: 晓晴，我们上周谈到了把自动化思维写下来的方法。这几天尝试得怎么样？有没有什么发现？
turns.belief_state: 作业能帮助来访者获得新的觉察

turns.speaker: client
turns.text: 老师，我试着写了两次，但写完之后我更难过了。我觉得自己在强行说服自己那些不真实的积极话语，这根本没用，反而觉得你在否定我的痛苦。
turns.belief_state: 咨询师不理解我，方法对我无效

turns.speaker: therapist
turns.text: 听到你这么说，我首先想向你道歉。我的本意是想帮你看到更多的可能性，但如果让你觉得我在强迫你乐观、甚至否定了你的痛苦，那真的是我的失误。我很感谢你愿意直接把这个感受告诉我。
turns.belief_state: 咨询中的误解需要及时修复，来访者的反馈至关重要

turns.speaker: client
turns.text: 我以为只要写下来就会变好，但现实是期中考试又要来了，那种焦虑感还是铺天盖地。我根本做不到去挑战那些想法。
turns.belief_state: 面对现实压力时，认知调整显得苍白无力

turns.speaker: therapist
turns.text: 你的感受完全可以理解。认知重构不是为了盲目乐观，也不是为了否定你的痛苦。既然思维记录让你觉得有压力，那我们今天换个角度，聊聊‘行为激活’。你觉得最近一周里，除了上课，有没有哪件哪怕很小的事，能让你稍微感觉有一点点掌控感？
turns.belief_state: 当认知调整受阻时，可以从行为层面切入

turns.speaker: client
turns.text: 掌控感？前天晚上室友拉我去操场散步了一圈，当时吹着风，好像没有在宿舍胡思乱想那么难受。
turns.belief_state: 微小的行动能带来情绪上的微调

turns.speaker: therapist
turns.text: 太棒了，这正是一个极好的切入点。散步并不是为了解决期末考试，但它实实在在地打破了你的回避循环。如果我们本周把这种小行动作为一个‘行为实验’，你愿意尝试吗？
turns.belief_state: 通过具体、小步的行为实验可以积累自我效能感

turns.speaker: client
turns.text: 只是散步的话，压力好像没有那么大。我可以试试每天晚上去走十五分钟。
turns.belief_state: 低压力的行为实验是可行的

sessions.ending_state: 成功修复了上一阶段的沟通误解，将来访者的注意力从高难度的认知重构转移到低压力的行为激活实验上。

sessions.goal: 评估行为实验的结果，并开始探讨隐藏在学业完美主义背后的深层信念。

turns.speaker: therapist
turns.text: 晓晴，上周我们约定了进行每天散步十五分钟的行为实验，这周的执行情况怎么样？
turns.belief_state: 行为实验的复盘有助于增强来访者的掌控感

turns.speaker: client
turns.text: 我坚持了四天。虽然期中成绩还是让我很焦虑，但散步的时候确实感觉脑子里没那么拥挤了。不过，我昨天没去，因为我觉得复习时间不够，去散步是在浪费时间，心里特别内疚。
turns.belief_state: 休息和放松就是浪费时间，必须把所有时间用于学习

turns.speaker: therapist
turns.text: 你看，‘散步是浪费时间’这个想法非常有意思。它背后似乎藏着一条更深的规则：‘如果我有一分钟不学习，我就是在走向失败。’你觉得这条规则平时在多大程度上统治着你的生活？
turns.belief_state: 表面现象下往往存在更核心的中间信念或规则

turns.speaker: client
turns.text: 从小到大，我爸妈就是这样对我的。他们常说‘不进则退’。如果我考了第二名，他们会问我为什么第一名不是我。我习惯了用成绩来证明自己的价值。
turns.belief_state: 我的价值完全取决于我的外部成就和父母的认可

turns.speaker: therapist
turns.text: 难怪你背负了这么重的担子。把自我价值和每一次考试结果紧紧绑定在一起，这意味着你永远不能真正放松，因为任何一次波动都成了生存危机。
turns.belief_state: 来访者的核心信念源于家庭环境的长期塑造

turns.speaker: client
turns.text: 对啊，我有时候真的很恨自己这么软弱，为什么不能像别人那样，及格就行？但我又做不到不在乎。
turns.belief_state: 无法接受不完美的自己

turns.speaker: therapist
turns.text: 这恰恰说明你在乎自己的未来，你有上进心。只是，我们需要把‘追求卓越’和‘自我毁灭式的完美主义’区分开。如果晓晴不是一个在成绩单上拿第一的学生，那她作为一个完整的人，还拥有哪些宝贵的品质呢？
turns.belief_state: 人的价值是多维度的，不应被单一标签定义

turns.speaker: client
turns.text: 品质吗……我觉得自己挺会倾听朋友的心事的，对人也真诚。但我不知道这些在大学里有什么用……
turns.belief_state: 开始尝试寻找除成绩之外的自我价值，但仍存有不确定性

sessions.ending_state: 深入探讨了家庭期望与核心信念对来访者的影响，虽然尚未彻底瓦解完美主义，但来访者开始意识到自我价值的多元可能性，咨询进入稳步推进阶段。

sessions.goal: Introduce the cognitive-behavioral model and map out the cycle of avoidance and loneliness.

turns.speaker: therapist
turns.text: Hello Sarah. Thank you for coming in today. Perhaps we can start by discussing what brings you here and what you hope to work on.
turns.belief_state: Establishing collaborative framework

turns.speaker: client
turns.text: Hi. I've just been feeling really isolated lately, but at the same time, whenever someone invites me out, I find myself making excuses not to go.
turns.belief_state: I am too exhausted to engage socially.

turns.speaker: therapist
turns.text: It sounds like there is a push and pull between wanting connection and feeling a strong urge to pull back. How do you usually make sense of that urge when it happens?
turns.belief_state: Avoidance serves a protective function for the client.

turns.speaker: client
turns.text: I usually think that if I go, I'll just be awkward, or they only invited me out of politeness anyway. So staying home feels safer.
turns.belief_state: My friends do not actually want to spend time with me.

turns.speaker: therapist
turns.text: That thought—that they only invited you out of politeness—seems to carry a lot of weight. If we look at how thoughts, feelings, and behaviors connect, what happens in your body when you think that?
turns.belief_state: Connecting thoughts to somatic and emotional responses.

turns.speaker: client
turns.text: I feel this heavy drop in my stomach, and then complete exhaustion. Like my energy just drains away immediately.
turns.belief_state: Physical depletion validates the desire to withdraw.

turns.speaker: therapist
turns.text: So the thought leads to physical heaviness and exhaustion, which then makes staying home feel like the only logical choice. But then, does staying home help with the loneliness?
turns.belief_state: Highlighting the maintenance cycle of avoidance.

turns.speaker: client
turns.text: Not really. It helps for about ten minutes, and then the loneliness just gets worse. It's like a trap.
turns.belief_state: Recognizing the paradoxical effect of avoidance.

sessions.ending_state: The client grasped the basic CBT formulation connecting thoughts of rejection to avoidance behaviors and subsequent loneliness.

sessions.goal: Examine automatic negative thoughts regarding friend interactions and design a behavioral experiment.

turns.speaker: therapist
turns.text: Welcome back, Sarah. How has your week been since we mapped out that cycle last time?
turns.belief_state: Checking in on interval learning

turns.speaker: client
turns.text: It was mixed. I noticed the cycle happening a lot. A friend texted me on Wednesday asking to grab coffee, and my immediate thought was 'she's just checking a box because she feels sorry for me.'
turns.belief_state: Friend's invitation is insincere.

turns.speaker: therapist
turns.text: And how did you respond to that text based on that thought?
turns.belief_state: Tracing behavior from automatic thought.

turns.speaker: client
turns.text: I waited a whole day to reply and then said I was swamped with work. Which wasn't entirely true. I felt guilty about lying, but relieved I didn't have to go.
turns.belief_state: Avoidance provides temporary relief paired with guilt.

turns.speaker: therapist
turns.text: So you managed the anxiety of the invitation by declining, but the cost was some guilt and missed connection. Would you be open to testing this belief that she was just 'checking a box'?
turns.belief_state: Proposing a behavioral experiment to test thoughts.

turns.speaker: client
turns.text: I don't know. How would we test that? Ask her outright if she feels sorry for me? That sounds terrifying and awkward.
turns.belief_state: Testing requires socially risky confrontation.

turns.speaker: therapist
turns.text: Ah, we definitely don't need to do something that uncomfortable right away. What if the experiment was simply accepting a low-stakes invitation or sending a short text first, and noticing the actual outcome versus your prediction?
turns.belief_state: Stepping down experiment difficulty to match client window of tolerance.

turns.speaker: client
turns.text: I suppose I could try sending a message to my friend Maya. We haven't spoken in a couple of weeks. But what if she ignores me?
turns.belief_state: Anticipating rejection.

sessions.ending_state: A minor rupture/hesitation regarding experiment design was resolved, setting up a milder behavioral test for the coming week.

sessions.goal: Review the behavioral experiment, address a misunderstanding about expectations, and refine coping strategies.

turns.speaker: therapist
turns.text: Hello Sarah. How did things go with Maya this week? Did you end up sending that message?
turns.belief_state: Following up on homework.

turns.speaker: client
turns.text: I did send it. But honestly, it didn't go the way I hoped, and I felt a bit let down by our session last week because I felt rushed into doing it.
turns.belief_state: Voicing therapeutic rupture.

turns.speaker: therapist
turns.text: I really appreciate you telling me that. I apologize if I pushed you too fast. Can you tell me what happened when you sent the message, and how you experienced my pacing?
turns.belief_state: Validating client feedback and repairing rupture.

turns.speaker: client
turns.text: Well, Maya replied, but she said she was busy that day and suggested another time next month. And my brain immediately went back to 'see, she's brushing you off.' But regarding here, I just felt like you wanted me to fix everything instantly.
turns.belief_state: Separating external reality from internal interpretation.

turns.speaker: therapist
turns.text: That makes total sense. When Maya suggested next month, your mind interpreted it as a brush-off rather than a scheduling conflict. And with me, it felt like pressure to perform rather than collaborate. That is extremely helpful data for us.
turns.belief_state: Reframing the experiment outcome as a cognitive distortion pattern.

turns.speaker: client
turns.text: Yeah. When I actually looked at her text without panicking, she offered two specific dates. That doesn't sound like someone trying to get rid of me.
turns.belief_state: Alternative evidence disconfirms automatic thought.

turns.speaker: therapist
turns.text: That is a huge distinction to catch. Notice how catching that alternative perspective changed your emotional state just now?
turns.belief_state: Consolidating cognitive shift.

turns.speaker: client
turns.text: It did. I feel lighter. But I'm still nervous about actually meeting up with her next month. We'll have to keep working on that anticipation anxiety.
turns.belief_state: Acknowledging ongoing work and client agency.

sessions.ending_state: Successful repair of a minor therapeutic rupture, realistic evaluation of experimental data, and continued planning for future social exposures.

sessions.goal: 建立咨询同盟，初步梳理成就与自我价值的关系，并确立核心评估方向。

turns.speaker: client
turns.text: 老师您好，其实我预约的时候心里很矛盾。我觉得自己不应该来做心理咨询，因为这点工作上的压力我都处理不好，实在太没用了。
turns.belief_state: 如果我的工作结果不够完美，我就是一个彻底的失败者。

turns.speaker: therapist
turns.text: 晓，欢迎你。听到你一进来就用“没用”来评价自己，我能感受到你背负着沉重的压力。我们要不要一起看看，是什么让你把工作上的挫折直接等同于你整个人的价值呢？
turns.belief_state: 客户将成就与自我价值高度绑定，需要通过协作打破这一自动思维。

turns.speaker: client
turns.text: 从小到大都是这样的。我妈常说，考不到第一名就等于白学。当上了设计主管后，底下的人做出来的东西达不到我的标准，我通宵帮他们改。我觉得全都是我的责任，如果团队业绩不好，就是我无能。
turns.belief_state: 我的价值完全取决于我能取得多少外界认可的成就。

turns.speaker: therapist
turns.text: 这听起来像是一个非常苛刻的规则：你必须永远完美，否则就是失败。而且你把团队所有人的表现都背在了你自己的肩上。这种信念在过去可能帮助你取得了许多成就，但也让你现在精疲力竭，对吗？
turns.belief_state: 识别出客户僵化的条件化假设及其高昂的情感代价。

turns.speaker: client
turns.text: 对，但我不知道还能怎么办。如果我不盯着，不做到最好，我就会觉得恐慌。我觉得只要稍微放松，我就会一无所有，被别人抛弃或者取代。
turns.belief_state: 只要稍微放松就会一无所有。

turns.speaker: therapist
turns.text: 这种“一无所有”的恐惧非常真实。我们接下来的几周，可以像科学家做实验一样，来看看这个规则到底在多大程度上保护了你，又在多大程度上伤害了你。你愿意和我们一起探索吗？
turns.belief_state: 引入CBT的协作性经验主义框架。

turns.speaker: client
turns.text: 做实验？我不知道怎么做……我只知道如果完不成目标，我就会陷入深深的自我否定。但我确实累了，我想试试看。
turns.belief_state: 客户展现出改变的意愿，但仍有防御。

turns.speaker: therapist
turns.text: 很好，今天我们先迈出第一步。接下来一周，你可以试着记录下当你在工作中感到焦虑时，脑子里具体闪过了哪些想法，我们下次见面时一起分析。
turns.belief_state: 布置第一次自我监测作业。

sessions.ending_state: 初步建立了协作同盟，识别出核心信念，客户同意开始进行自动化思维的自我监测。

sessions.goal: 回顾认知日志，探讨完美主义的双向影响，并识别“全或无”的思维谬误。

turns.speaker: therapist
turns.text: 晓，你好。过去一周的监测记录带给你什么新的发现吗？
turns.belief_state: 期待通过客户的自我观察促进认知重构。

turns.speaker: client
turns.text: 我记了几天。结果让我挺意外的。比如周三，下属交上来的初稿其实没有我想象的那么糟，但我还是忍不住挑了十几个毛病。记录的时候我才发现，我好像根本不允许别人出错，也绝对不允许自己出错。
turns.belief_state: 开始觉察到自己对完美主义的执念不仅针对自己，也投射到他人身上。

turns.speaker: therapist
turns.text: 这是一个非常深刻的觉察。当你必须在所有事情上都追求完美时，你觉得这给你和你的团队带来了什么样的后果？
turns.belief_state: 引导客户评估成本与收益。

turns.speaker: client
turns.text: 后果就是大家都很紧绷，我自己也连续几天失眠。但是……（停顿）如果不这样，万一客户不满意呢？万一公司觉得我不适合这个职位呢？那我所有的努力不就白费了吗？
turns.belief_state: 如果我不完美，就会面临灾难性的职业否定。

turns.speaker: therapist
turns.text: 我听到这里有一个假设：只要有一处不完美，就会导致全局的溃败，这就是我们常说的“全或无”思维。晓，有没有可能，一个设计或者一个人，可以在某些地方不够完美，但依然是有价值、有能力的呢？
turns.belief_state: 挑战绝对化与全或无的认知偏差。

turns.speaker: client
turns.text: 理智上我觉得有可能，但我做不到。如果我承认自己有做不好的地方，那就证明我能力不够。这是我绝对不能接受的。
turns.belief_state: 旧有防御机制因触及核心情感而产生小幅波动。

turns.speaker: therapist
turns.text: 我能感受到你内心的防线保护得很紧，这没关系。我们不需要立刻推翻它。我们可以把这个想法当作一个假设，而不是绝对的事实，接下来我们试着设计一个小实验来检验它？
turns.belief_state: 处理咨询中的轻微防御，维持协作关系。

turns.speaker: client
turns.text: 什么实验？如果实验失败了怎么办？
turns.belief_state: 对行为实验结果充满焦虑。

turns.speaker: therapist
turns.text: 实验的意义就在于，无论结果如何，我们都能学到东西，而不会对你的人格产生任何贬低。我们可以尝试在一项非核心任务中，故意保留一个微小的、不完美的细节，看看会发生什么。
turns.belief_state: 设计低风险的行为实验。

turns.speaker: client
turns.text: 好吧……听起来挺冒险的，但我愿意试试看。
turns.belief_state: 客户同意进行第一次行为实验。

sessions.ending_state: 识别出“全或无”思维，虽然遭遇轻微防御与抗拒，但在咨询师温和引导下同意开展行为实验。

sessions.goal: 评估行为实验结果，处理实验带来的焦虑与误解，探索替代性核心信念。

turns.speaker: therapist
turns.text: 晓，上次我们谈到要进行一个“故意不完美”的小实验。这周进展得怎么样？
turns.belief_state: 关注行为实验的实施情况及其心理冲击。

turns.speaker: client
turns.text: 老师，我必须跟你说，我上周没做好。我觉得你根本不理解我有多大压力。你让我故意不完美，但我交上去的那份方案被老板指出了一个小瑕疵，我当时整个人差点崩溃，我觉得你当时给我的建议太轻率了！
turns.belief_state: 产生咨询小裂痕，认为咨询师不理解其处境。

turns.speaker: therapist
turns.text: 听到你这么说，我首先向你道歉，如果我的建议让你觉得被轻视或者承受了额外的痛苦。我的确没有完全体会到那个瑕疵带给你的真实冲击。你能跟我多说说当时发生了什么吗？
turns.belief_state: 及时修复咨询关系，将情绪转为可探索的素材。

turns.speaker: client
turns.text: （叹气）其实老板也就是随口提了一句，让我下次注意。但我当时脑子里全是：你看，我就说吧，不完美就会完蛋！我觉得你好像在拿我的职业生涯开玩笑……
turns.belief_state: 老板的轻描淡写与内心的灾难化预期形成强烈反差。

turns.speaker: therapist
turns.text: 谢谢你坦诚地告诉我这些。我们来看刚才这个过程：老板的反馈是“随口提了一句，让你下次注意”，但你的大脑把它自动翻译成了“完蛋了”。这两者之间，是不是有些微妙的距离？
turns.belief_state: 利用具体事件区分客观现实与灾难化认知。

turns.speaker: client
turns.text: 好像……确实是这样。老板并没有生气，也没有开除我。但我当时那种心跳加速、世界要塌下来的感觉太真实了，我没办法控制它。
turns.belief_state: 认知与躯体反应存在分离。

turns.speaker: therapist
turns.text: 身体的生理反应是真实的，因为它习惯了把任何小瑕疵都当作最高等级的威胁。但这次实验也向我们证明了一点：即使有不完美的地方，天也没有塌下来。这算不算是一个意料之外的发现？
turns.belief_state: 总结行为实验的建设性成果。

turns.speaker: client
turns.text: （苦笑）对，好像事实并没有我想象的那么可怕。但我心里的那个声音还是在说，这次只是运气好。
turns.belief_state: 核心信念开始松动，但旧信念仍在抵抗。

turns.speaker: therapist
turns.text: 没关系，能听到“运气好”这种解释很正常。这说明我们的旧信念非常顽固。但至少我们看到，除了成就之外，你的世界并没有因为一次小瑕疵而毁灭。接下来，我们可以试着为自己写一句新的座右铭了。
turns.belief_state: 准备进入构建替代性核心信念的阶段。

turns.speaker: client
turns.text: 新的座右铭……也许我可以试着接受，我是一个有能力的人，即使偶尔出错，也不影响我的整体价值？
turns.belief_state: 初步形成多元自我价值的替代性信念。

sessions.ending_state: 成功处理了咨询过程中的关系裂痕，通过复盘行为实验，客户的灾难化认知得到松动，并开始尝试构建替代性信念。

sessions.goal: Establish collaborative framework and explore the presenting problem of perceived professional inadequacy.

turns.speaker: therapist

turns.belief_state: neutral

turns.speaker: client

turns.speaker: therapist

turns.text: I just picture myself packing up my desk while everyone looks at me with disappointment.

turns.speaker: therapist
turns.text: So a revision on a layout triggers a vivid picture of absolute rejection. Would it be alright if we map out how this thought connects to your emotions and physical reactions?
turns.belief_state: cbt formulation model

turns.speaker: client
turns.text: We can try, but honestly, I think it is just the truth. I am not cut out for this field.

turns.text: I appreciate your honesty. Let's treat that idea as a hypothesis rather than an absolute fact, and look at the evidence together over the next few weeks.

sessions.goal: Examine automatic thoughts regarding peer interactions and design a behavioral experiment.

turns.speaker: therapist
turns.text: Welcome back, Elena. How has your week been since we spoke about tracking your automatic thoughts?
turns.belief_state: neutral

turns.speaker: client
turns.text: I tried writing them down, but it just made me realize how broken my thinking is. I had a lunch invitation from a coworker and immediately assumed she only asked because she felt sorry for me.

turns.speaker: therapist

turns.belief_state: behavioral experiment design

turns.speaker: client
turns.text: I suppose I could accept an invitation without analyzing every word she says, or even initiate coffee myself.
turns.belief_state: exploring agency

turns.speaker: therapist
turns.text: That sounds like a meaningful behavioral experiment. How does your body feel when you imagine initiating coffee?
turns.belief_state: somatic check-in

turns.speaker: client
turns.text: My chest tightens, but underneath, there is a tiny spark of excitement. I guess I am tired of hiding.
turns.belief_state: readiness for change

sessions.ending_state: Identified a concrete behavioral experiment to test coworker intentions and addressed self-critical judgment of thoughts.

sessions.goal: Review the behavioral experiment, address a minor therapeutic rupture regarding perceived pushiness, and update core beliefs.

turns.speaker: therapist
turns.text: Hello Elena. How did the experiment go with your coworker this week?
turns.belief_state: neutral

turns.speaker: client
turns.text: I actually did ask her for coffee. It went fine, but honestly, when you pushed me to do it last time, I felt like you didn't understand how terrifying it is for me.

turns.speaker: therapist
turns.text: I am so glad you told me that. I moved too quickly and sounded directive rather than collaborative. Thank you for holding me accountable.
turns.belief_state: repairing alliance

turns.speaker: client
turns.text: I wasn't expecting you to agree with me so easily. Usually, people just defend themselves when I speak up.
turns.belief_state: people can be receptive

turns.speaker: therapist
turns.text: Your perspective matters here. Now, putting aside my misstep for a moment, what happened during the coffee date?
turns.belief_state: returning to client data

turns.belief_state: People might enjoy my presence.

turns.text: That is a powerful piece of counter-evidence against the old belief. What does that tell you about your underlying assumptions?
turns.belief_state: core belief examination

turns.speaker: therapist

turns.belief_state: 区分客观反馈与主观全或无认知

turns.speaker: client
turns.text: 我知道理智上是这样，但情感上做不到。我觉得只要有一点瑕疵，就是我能力不够的铁证。我从小受到的教育就是，考99分是不够的，必须得是100分。

turns.speaker: client
turns.text: （沉默了几秒）画下来？好吧。其实它保护我没有在小时候挨批评，但现在它让我每时每刻都处在备战状态，太累了。

turns.text: 实地调查？听起来有点像要我去冒险。你要让我去公司当众演讲吗？我可做不到。

turns.belief_state: 尊重来访者边界，循序渐进暴露

turns.speaker: client
turns.text: 停顿五秒钟？天哪，那五秒钟对我来说会像一个世纪那么长。万一别人觉得我脑子卡壳了怎么办？
turns.belief_state: 短暂的停顿会被灾难化解读

turns.speaker: therapist
turns.text: 这正是我们想检验的假设：‘别人会立刻觉得你脑子卡壳并嫌弃你’。如果我们在一个相对安全的场景，比如和小范围的亲友或者合伙人先试一下呢？
turns.belief_state: 通过可控环境降低焦虑门槛

turns.speaker: client
turns.text: 嗯……如果只是和我伴侣的话，我倒是可以试试。反正他平时也经常看我出丑。周末我可以试着在聊天时故意停顿，看看他真实的反应是什么，而不是我去猜。
turns.belief_state: 愿意将实验范围缩小至安全社交圈

turns.belief_state: 记录实证数据能有效修正偏误

turns.speaker: client
turns.text: 好，那我回去试一试。虽然我还是有点心虚，但我愿意看看自己是不是又在胡思乱想了。
turns.belief_state: 开始尝试对自我自动化思维进行元认知监控

sessions.ending_state: 成功协商并确定了第一个微型行为实验的方案，来访者从最初的抗拒转为谨慎的愿意尝试。

sessions.goal: Establish collaborative case conceptualization, identify automatic thoughts surrounding physiological arousal, and set baseline monitoring.

turns.speaker: therapist
turns.text: Hello Julian. It is good to meet you today. As we begin, I want to make sure we work together as a team to understand what brings you in and what you would like to get out of our time.
turns.belief_state: Collaboration is essential for effective exploration.

turns.speaker: client
turns.text: Thanks for seeing me. I am here because I feel completely exhausted by my own body. Whenever my heart rate picks up, even just from walking fast, my mind immediately goes to the worst-case scenario: that something is terribly wrong physically.
turns.belief_state: If my heart rate goes up unexpectedly, it means my body is failing.

turns.speaker: therapist
turns.text: That sounds incredibly draining, having to police your own physical sensations all the time. When you notice that heart rate increase and the thought that something is wrong arises, what typically happens next?
turns.belief_state: Understanding the cognitive chain will reveal maintaining factors.

turns.speaker: client
turns.text: I immediately sit down, try to slow my breathing, and check my pulse on my wrist or neck. I scan myself continuously to see if the tightness in my chest is getting worse.
turns.belief_state: I must constantly monitor my physical sensations to ensure I am safe.

turns.speaker: therapist
turns.text: So checking and monitoring become the main actions you take. Let's look at that together. How well has that constant monitoring worked to reduce your long-term worry?
turns.belief_state: Behavioral experiments can test the utility of safety strategies.

turns.speaker: client
turns.text: Honestly, it hasn't worked. It feels like the more I check, the more I find things to worry about. But if I don't check, I feel like I am taking a massive risk.
turns.belief_state: Stopping monitoring feels dangerous, but continuing it keeps me trapped.

turns.speaker: therapist
turns.text: That is a really important insight. We are noticing a paradox: the safety behavior of monitoring might actually be fueling the alarm. Would you be willing to treat that as a hypothesis we can test together rather than a strict rule?
turns.belief_state: Viewing thoughts and behaviors as hypotheses reduces rigidity.

turns.speaker: client
turns.text: I can see the logic, but it feels scary to imagine not checking my pulse when I feel tight in the chest. I am not sure I am ready to just drop it completely.
turns.belief_state: The client experiences a boundary regarding pacing and readiness.

turns.speaker: therapist
turns.text: We certainly do not have to drop it today. We go at your pace. For this week, would you be open simply to logging these episodes when they occur, noting the thought and the urge to check, without necessarily forcing yourself to change the behavior yet?
turns.belief_state: Collaborative pacing preserves the therapeutic alliance and fosters agency.

sessions.ending_state: Julian agreed to maintain a thought and behavior log focusing on physiological sensations and monitoring urges, establishing a baseline without feeling pushed into premature behavioral change.

sessions.goal: Review the self-monitoring log, examine evidence for and against catastrophic appraisals, and design a mild behavioral experiment.

turns.speaker: therapist
turns.text: Welcome back, Julian. How was your week, and what did you notice as you filled out the monitoring logs?
turns.belief_state: Reviewing data collaboratively enhances self-discovery.

turns.speaker: client
turns.text: It was eye-opening in some ways, but also frustrating. I noticed I checked my pulse at least twenty times a day. Every time I felt a flutter, I thought: 'This is it, cardiac event.' But nothing actually happened; the feeling just passed on its own after a few minutes.
turns.belief_state: Data collection shows that catastrophic predictions do not materialize.

turns.speaker: therapist
turns.text: That is fascinating data you gathered yourself. Notice how every single time you predicted disaster, the prediction did not come true, even though the physical sensation felt very real.
turns.belief_state: Distinguishing between physical sensations and catastrophic interpretations is crucial.

turns.speaker: client
turns.text: Yeah, logically I see that. But when I am in the moment, the logic flies out the window. My brain tells me: 'Well, you got lucky this time, but next time will be different.'
turns.belief_state: The cognitive shift is intellectually acknowledged but emotionally resisted.

turns.speaker: therapist
turns.text: That 'next time' argument is very common. It keeps the anxiety loop running. Since your own log showed that sensations rise and fall on their own, would you be willing to test what happens if you intentionally bring on a mild physical sensation—like walking briskly up a flight of stairs—and deliberately delay checking your pulse for two minutes?
turns.belief_state: Behavioral experiments provide experiential disconfirmation of beliefs.

turns.speaker: client
turns.text: Wait, you want me to deliberately make my heart beat faster? That sounds like asking for trouble. What if I trigger a full panic attack right here or on the way home?
turns.belief_state: Fear of the experiment itself creates a rupture in perceived safety.

turns.speaker: therapist
turns.text: I hear your concern, and I appreciate you being direct about how frightening that sounds. We certainly would not do anything unsafe, and we can control the intensity. But if we only talk about it, your brain never gets the chance to learn that increased heart rate can be safe. How can we modify this experiment so it feels manageable?
turns.belief_state: Addressing resistance collaboratively without forcing compliance is vital.

turns.speaker: client
turns.text: I suppose if we do it right here in the room, where I know I am safe and you are here, I might consider doing a minute of jumping jacks or fast stepping. But I still feel like this is a risky idea.
turns.belief_state: Client exercises agency by modifying the experiment's parameters.

turns.speaker: therapist
turns.text: Doing it right here together sounds like a solid modification. We are in control of the dosage. Let's examine what you predict will happen if you do one minute of fast stepping right now.
turns.belief_state: Collaborative formulation of the in-session experiment ensures buy-in.

sessions.ending_state: Julian agreed to an in-session behavioral experiment involving controlled physical exertion, though underlying apprehension regarding bodily arousal remained unresolved.

sessions.goal: Execute the in-session behavioral experiment, process the experiential learning, and address broader beliefs about public judgment and perceived weakness.

turns.speaker: therapist
turns.text: Hello Julian. Today, keeping in mind our discussion last week, we have the option to run the brief physical exertion experiment we designed. How are you feeling about that today?
turns.belief_state: Checking in before action maintains client autonomy.

turns.speaker: client
turns.text: I thought about it all week. My stomach was in knots thinking about it, but I also realized I am tired of being afraid of my own heartbeat. Let's do it.
turns.belief_state: Motivation to overcome avoidance outweighs the fear of discomfort.

turns.speaker: therapist
turns.text: That takes a lot of courage. Let's rate your anxiety right now from zero to ten, do one minute of fast stepping in place, and then track how your body responds without checking your pulse during the minute.
turns.belief_state: Structuring the experiment provides a container for distress.

turns.speaker: client
turns.text: Okay, my anxiety is at a 6 right now just thinking about starting. Here goes.
turns.belief_state: Anticipatory anxiety is high.

turns.speaker: therapist
turns.text: [After one minute of fast stepping] Good job. Now, let's sit down, notice what your heart is doing, and rate the anxiety and physical sensations without reaching for your wrist.
turns.belief_state: Post-experiment processing consolidates learning.

turns.speaker: client
turns.text: My heart is pounding, definitely. My chest feels a bit tight. But... I notice I am not passing out. The pounding is just what happens when you move fast. It is actually quite normal.
turns.belief_state: Experiential data contradicts the catastrophic prediction.

turns.speaker: therapist
turns.text: Notice that. Your body did exactly what a healthy human body does when exerting itself: it increased circulation. What does that tell you about your prediction that heart rate means failure?
turns.belief_state: Guiding the client to draw their own conclusions strengthens cognitive restructuring.

turns.speaker: client
turns.text: It tells me my alarm system is overly sensitive. It is treating normal function like an emergency. But I still worry about what would happen if someone saw me like this in public—if I looked out of breath or weak during a meeting.
turns.belief_state: If I lose control of my body in public, others will judge me as weak and incapable.

turns.speaker: therapist
turns.text: That brings up another core layer: the fear of social evaluation and appearing weak, which connects back to your family background of pushing through exhaustion. We have made great progress on the physical side today, and we now have a clear opening to examine these social concerns in our next sessions.
turns.belief_state: Connecting present symptoms to deeper schemas prepares the ground for future work.

sessions.ending_state: Julian successfully completed the in-session behavioral experiment, disconfirming the belief that elevated heart rate equals physical failure, while uncovering the adjacent core belief regarding social evaluation and perceived weakness.

sessions.goal: 识别并梳理近期财务挫折引发的自动思维与情绪反应

turns.speaker: client
turns.text: 老师，我最近真的快撑不下去了。支票被退回的那一刻，我感觉自己像个彻头彻尾的失败者。

turns.speaker: therapist

turns.speaker: client
turns.text: 我脑子里就是一片空白，然后一直在想：完了，我这条自由职业的路彻底没希望了，父母以前说得对，我就是不适合干这个。

turns.speaker: therapist
turns.text: 这是一个非常沉重的想法。当你想着‘这条路彻底没希望了’的时候，它带给你的情绪是什么样的？

turns.speaker: client
turns.text: 就是绝望，觉得做什么都没用了，甚至连起身的力气都没有。
turns.belief_state: 我被困在这个绝望的情境里出不去了。

turns.speaker: therapist
turns.text: 这让我们看到，想法和情绪之间有着很强的连结。我们是不是可以把这些想法当作临时的假设，而不是百分之百的事实来审视？
turns.belief_state: 自动思维不等同于客观现实。

turns.speaker: client
turns.text: 话是这么说，可事实就是钱没了，客户跑了，这怎么能只是假设呢？
turns.belief_state: 咨询师可能无法真正体会我的经济压力。

turns.speaker: therapist
turns.text: 我能感受到你的质疑，这确实是极具挑战的现实。我的意思是，财务上的挫折和‘整条路都没希望了’，之间可能存在一段距离。今天我们可以一起看看这中间发生了什么。
turns.belief_state: 修复潜在的微小误解，保持合作同盟。

sessions.ending_state: 来访者表达了对思维与事实区分的防御，但初步建立起共同探讨的意愿，情绪在倾听下略有平复。

sessions.goal: 检验‘我什么都做不好’的绝对化信念，寻找反证

turns.speaker: client
turns.text: 上次回去后我想了想，觉得你可能觉得我在无理取闹，但我确实很难不去想那些糟糕的结果。
turns.belief_state: 我的负面情绪可能会让咨询师失望。

turns.speaker: therapist
turns.text: 谢谢你坦诚地告诉我这些。我想澄清的是，没有任何‘无理取闹’，你的担忧在这里是完全被允许的。今天我们愿意花时间看看你过去成功应对财务小危机的经验吗？
turns.belief_state: 建立安全、非评判的探索空间。

turns.speaker: client
turns.text: 成功经验？去年其实也有个客户拖欠尾款，后来我通过发律师函和分期催收要回来了。但这能说明什么呢？这不代表我这次就能做好。
turns.belief_state: 过去的成功只是运气，不能证明我的综合能力。

turns.speaker: therapist
turns.text: 它至少说明，你过去面对过类似困难，并且采取了有效的行动。这和你的绝对化想法‘我什么都做不好’是否有一点点出入？
turns.belief_state: 通过行为证据挑战全或无的认知模式。

turns.speaker: client
turns.text: 好像……确实有点矛盾。当时我挺勇敢的，现在怎么一遇到支票退回就吓成这样？
turns.belief_state: 或许我并非完全无能，只是这次被恐惧压垮了。

turns.speaker: therapist
turns.text: 因为这次支票退回触碰了你对未来的深层焦虑，特别是你提到父母对你自由职业的看法。这让压力倍增了。
turns.belief_state: 家庭期待加剧了来访者的无价值感。

turns.speaker: client
turns.text: 对，我总觉得一旦失败，就印证了他们是对的，我就是个没用的废人。
turns.belief_state: 我必须满足父母的期待才能证明自己的价值。

turns.speaker: therapist
turns.text: 听起来，你背负着双重压力：既要应对眼前的财务，还要背负证明给父母看的重担。这实在太累了。我们能不能把证明给别人看的任务先放下，看看你作为独立个体真正需要什么？

sessions.ending_state: 来访者开始辨认出过往的应对资源，并触及了家庭期待对自身认知的影响，情绪从防御转为深度的内省。

sessions.goal: 制定切实可行的应对行为实验，评估并恢复代理感

turns.speaker: client
turns.text: 这几天我试着把眼前的账目一条条列出来，虽然看着还是头疼，但好像没有想象中那么黑云压顶了。
turns.belief_state: 我其实有能力直面问题，哪怕过程很艰难。

turns.speaker: therapist
turns.text: 太棒了，看到你主动去梳理账目，这本身就是一个非常了不起的行动。你有什么新的发现吗？

turns.speaker: client
turns.text: 我发现其实有些款项是可以跟客户协商分期支付的，并不是所有人都打算赖账。不过我还是担心别人会看不起我主动催款的样子。
turns.emotional_state: 谨慎的希望与些许羞怯
turns.belief_state: 主动维护权益可能会遭到别人的负面评价。

turns.speaker: therapist
turns.text: 这是一个很好的切入点。我们可以设计一个小小的‘行为实验’：下周试着联系其中一位客户，看看真实反馈是否真的如你所担心的那样糟糕。
turns.belief_state: 通过现实检验来更新对社交和财务风险的预测。

turns.speaker: client
turns.text: 如果对方态度很恶劣怎么办？我怕我当场就接不住了。
turns.belief_state: 我无法承受他人可能的敌意。

turns.speaker: therapist
turns.text: 那我们在咨询室里先进行一次情境模拟，我扮演客户，你来练习如何温和而坚决地沟通，好吗？
turns.belief_state: 角色扮演能有效降低实际面对时的焦虑。

turns.speaker: client
turns.text: 行，那我们试试。其实我也想知道自己能不能硬气一次。
turns.belief_state: 我愿意为自己的改变做出尝试。

turns.speaker: therapist
turns.text: 很好，记住无论模拟结果如何，这都只是我们探索的一步，你已经展现出了非常宝贵的自主性。
turns.belief_state: 巩固来访者的自主权与阶段性成果。

sessions.ending_state: 来访者展现出更高的参与度和自主意愿，通过行为实验的构想与角色扮演准备，为接下来的现实行动奠定了基础。

sessions.goal: Establish collaborative framework, explore presenting problem of low self-efficacy, and identify initial automatic thoughts.

turns.speaker: therapist
turns.text: Hello Elena, welcome. I am glad we are meeting today. Where would you like to start?
turns.belief_state: Therapy is a collaborative journey.

turns.speaker: client
turns.text: Hi. Honestly, I am feeling a bit nervous. I was not even sure I should book this, because my problems are not really severe—I just feel like I am constantly failing at my design job.
turns.belief_state: My problems might not be important enough for therapy.

turns.speaker: therapist
turns.text: It is completely normal to feel uncertain about starting therapy. When you say you feel like you are constantly failing, what does that look like day-to-day?
turns.belief_state: Understanding specific examples will help clarify the core issue.

turns.speaker: client
turns.text: Well, yesterday my supervisor suggested a minor color adjustment on a layout, and immediately my mind went to: 'I am totally incompetent, they are going to figure out I don't belong here.'
turns.belief_state: If I make a mistake, it proves I cannot do anything right.

turns.speaker: therapist
turns.text: That sounds like a very heavy weight to carry over a routine revision. Notice how a minor suggestion instantly translated into a conclusion about your entire competence. Does that happen often?
turns.belief_state: Automatic thoughts are driving her emotional distress.

turns.speaker: client
turns.text: All the time. And even when something goes well, like when a client praises my work, I just think they are being polite or it was pure luck.
turns.belief_state: My successes are merely flukes.

turns.speaker: therapist
turns.text: So we have a pattern where negative feedback confirms your worst fears, and positive feedback gets discounted as luck. How does that sound as a starting map for our work together?
turns.belief_state: Co-creating a formulation empowers the client.

turns.speaker: client
turns.text: It sounds accurate, but it also feels a bit overwhelming to think I might have to change how my brain works entirely.
turns.belief_state: Change is daunting.

turns.speaker: therapist
turns.text: We do not have to change everything at once. For this week, let us just practice noticing when these thoughts pop up, without judging yourself for having them.
turns.belief_state: Small, manageable steps reduce anxiety about change.

turns.speaker: client
turns.text: Okay, I can try keeping a little log of those moments. That feels doable.
turns.belief_state: I can manage a small tracking task.

sessions.ending_state: Initial rapport established, automatic thought tracking agreed upon as a homework assignment.

sessions.goal: Review thought logs, examine intermediate beliefs about perfection, and address a minor therapeutic rupture regarding perceived judgment.

turns.speaker: therapist
turns.text: Welcome back, Elena. How did the week go with the thought log?
turns.belief_state: Reviewing homework provides direct data for cognitive work.

turns.speaker: client
turns.text: I filled it out, but honestly, looking at it made me feel pretty stupid. I wrote down things that seem so trivial now. I felt like you were going to judge me for being overly sensitive.
turns.belief_state: My thoughts are foolish and others will judge me.

turns.speaker: therapist
turns.text: I really appreciate you sharing that fear of being judged. Let us pause right there—what makes you worry that I would judge you for your thoughts?
turns.belief_state: Addressing the rupture immediately strengthens the therapeutic alliance.

turns.speaker: client
turns.text: Because growing up, any time I expressed self-doubt, my parents would say I was just making excuses or lacking mental toughness. I expect everyone to react that way.
turns.belief_state: Showing vulnerability leads to criticism.

turns.speaker: therapist
turns.text: That makes total sense given your background. If you were conditioned to expect harsh criticism for doubting yourself, of course you would brace for it here. But I am not here to grade your logs; we are examining them together as a team.
turns.belief_state: Connecting past conditioning to present fears helps de-escalate anxiety.

turns.speaker: client
turns.text: Thank you. Hearing that helps. Looking at one entry from Tuesday, I wrote: 'If the client asks for revisions, it means my initial design was garbage.'
turns.belief_state: Revisions equal total failure.

turns.speaker: therapist
turns.text: Let us examine that belief. If a client asks for a revision, is it always true that the original work was garbage, or are there other reasons clients request changes?
turns.belief_state: Guided discovery helps uncover cognitive distortions.

turns.speaker: client
turns.text: I suppose sometimes their own preferences change, or they want to see a different direction. But my immediate reflex is still all-or-nothing.
turns.belief_state: Alternative explanations exist, but old habits persist.

turns.speaker: therapist
turns.text: Recognizing that reflex is a huge step. How might we test this assumption during your design projects this coming week?
turns.belief_state: Behavioral experiments solidify cognitive shifts.

turns.speaker: client
turns.text: Maybe I could ask a colleague for their honest take on a draft before I submit it, just to see if they think it is 'garbage' or just normal work.
turns.belief_state: I can test my assumptions through external feedback.

sessions.ending_state: Rupture successfully resolved through openness; behavioral experiment planned to test the all-or-nothing belief about revisions.

sessions.goal: Evaluate the behavioral experiment, explore core beliefs regarding inherent incompetence, and design a deeper cognitive restructuring exercise.

turns.speaker: therapist
turns.text: How did the experiment go this week? Did you manage to check in with a colleague?
turns.belief_state: Reviewing behavioral experiments provides concrete counter-evidence.

turns.speaker: client
turns.text: I did! I showed my draft to Mark, and instead of telling me it was terrible, he said it looked great and just suggested swapping one font. I was kind of stunned.
turns.belief_state: My work is not always terrible when revisions are requested.

turns.speaker: therapist
turns.text: Stunned in a good way, I hope? What did that experience tell you about your belief that any feedback means total incompetence?
turns.belief_state: Highlighting disconfirming evidence strengthens adaptive beliefs.

turns.speaker: client
turns.text: It told me my brain jumps to conclusions very quickly. But even though Mark liked it, a part of me still thinks, 'Well, Mark is just being nice, he doesn't want to hurt my feelings.'
turns.belief_state: Positive feedback can always be explained away.

turns.speaker: therapist
turns.text: Ah, the old discount rule at work. Whenever positive evidence appears, the mind finds a way to neutralize it. Why is it so hard to accept that you might have simply done a good job?
turns.belief_state: Uncovering the underlying core belief maintains momentum.

turns.speaker: client
turns.text: Because if I admit I am good at something, then I have to maintain that standard. And if I fail later, it hurts so much more than if I just expect myself to fail from the start.
turns.belief_state: Expecting failure is a protective shield against disappointment.

turns.speaker: therapist
turns.text: That is such a profound insight, Elena. You are using low self-expectations as an armor to protect yourself from future disappointment. But what is that armor costing you day-to-day?
turns.belief_state: Examining the cost of maintaining core beliefs promotes motivation for change.

turns.speaker: client
turns.text: It costs me my peace of mind. I am exhausted from constantly bracing for a catastrophe that rarely actually happens.
turns.belief_state: The protective shield is actually exhausting.

turns.speaker: therapist
turns.text: Exhausted is a very honest place to start building something new. For our next step, let us look at constructing a core belief worksheet where we list evidence for and against your belief that you are inherently incompetent.
turns.belief_state: Systematic evaluation of core beliefs leads to cognitive restructuring.

turns.speaker: client
turns.text: Okay. I think I am ready to look at that evidence, even if it feels a little uncomfortable.
turns.belief_state: I am willing to tolerate discomfort for personal growth.

sessions.ending_state: Explored the function of low expectations as a protective shield; agreed to begin a core belief evaluation protocol.

sessions.goal: 建立咨询同盟并探索萨莉当前的自动思维与抑郁体验

turns.speaker: therapist
turns.text: 萨莉你好，非常欢迎你来到这里。我知道迈出这一步并不容易，我想先听听看，今天是什么促使你决定来找我的？
turns.belief_state: 建立安全合作的同盟是有效干预的基础

turns.speaker: client
turns.text: 我其实挺犹豫要不要来的。我觉得自己挺没用的，连大学生活都适应不好，每天除了呆在宿舍上网，什么都不想做。可是室友和家里人都在催我振作，我快撑不下去了。
turns.belief_state: 我是一个彻底的失败者，我什么事情都做不对

turns.speaker: therapist
turns.text: 听到你承受了这么大的压力，而且觉得周围的期待让你喘不过气来。我想确认一下，你刚才提到快撑不下去了，这其中包含伤害自己的念头吗？
turns.belief_state: 安全评估与人身保障永远是首要原则

turns.speaker: client
turns.text: 没有想过去死，我只是觉得活着太累了，每天都像是在应付差事。那种感觉就像掉进黑洞里，爬不出来。
turns.belief_state: 别人看起来都游刃有余，只有我是个异类

turns.speaker: therapist
turns.text: 谢谢你的坦诚。这种看不到出路的疲惫感确实非常消耗你。在接下来的时间里，我们不需要马上解决所有问题，而是试着像两个探险者一样，看看这个黑洞里到底有些什么想法在拉着你下坠。
turns.belief_state: 通过协作探索来拆解复杂的抑郁情绪

turns.speaker: client
turns.text: 探险？我连出门上课都觉得别人在盯着我看，觉得他们一定在嘲笑我的成绩和现在的样子。
turns.belief_state: 别人都在评判我，向别人倾诉只会显出软弱

turns.speaker: therapist
turns.text: 这种‘别人都在评判我’的想法听起来让你非常难受和孤立。这是我们常说的‘自动思维’。如果我们把这个想法写下来，看看它在多大程度上影响了你的行动，你觉得怎么样？
turns.belief_state: 识别自动思维是CBT的切入点

turns.speaker: client
turns.text: 写下来……好吧，反正我也没什么可失去的了。但我怀疑这真的有用吗？
turns.belief_state: 我不相信这种方法能改变我的现状

sessions.ending_state: 建立了初步信任，识别了核心的自动思维，但客户仍带有明显的怀疑和防御情绪。

sessions.goal: 检验‘失败者’的认知，探讨行为退缩与情绪低落的恶性循环

turns.speaker: therapist
turns.text: 萨莉，距离我们上次见面已经过去一周了。这段时间里，你过得怎么样？
turns.belief_state: 回顾一周进展有助于评估干预效果

turns.speaker: client
turns.text: 老实说，不是很好。我上周尝试按照我们说的方法记录想法，但我发现我根本记录不过来，因为我的脑子里全都是‘我搞砸了’。我还缺席了两节早课。
turns.belief_state: 我连记录想法都做不好，我真的是无药可救了

turns.speaker: therapist
turns.text: 听起来你对自己的要求很高，当记录没有达到完美时，反而成了新的压力源。这其实也反映出我们上周提到的那个信念：只要有一点做不好，就觉得自己彻底失败了。
turns.belief_state: 全或无的思维方式在驱动当前的沮丧

turns.speaker: client
turns.text: 可是事实就是这样啊！期末考试考砸了，现在连课都去不了，这不是失败是什么？你是在安慰我吗？
turns.belief_state: 咨询师可能根本不懂我的痛苦，只是在说客套话

turns.speaker: therapist
turns.text: 我能感受到你现在的防御和质疑，这完全可以理解。我不是在用空洞的话安慰你，而是想邀请你一起看一看：当我们把‘期末一门课考砸’等同于‘我整个人都是失败者’时，这个结论中间是不是漏掉了很多其他可能？
turns.belief_state: 通过苏格拉底式提问促进认知重构

turns.speaker: client
turns.text: 还能有什么可能？成绩就是唯一的标准，在我家里就是这样的。
turns.belief_state: 家庭价值观深深束缚了我的自我评价

turns.speaker: therapist
turns.text: 我听到家庭的期待对你影响很深。如果我们做一个小实验，把‘一次考试的失利’和‘你作为一个人的价值’暂时分开，看看除了学习，你身上还有哪些特质或努力是考试分数无法衡量的？
turns.belief_state: 行为与认知实验能够松动绝对化信念

turns.speaker: client
turns.text: 特质？我不知道……我只知道我很擅长逃避。不过，我上周其实帮高中朋友梳理了一篇论文大纲，当时觉得还挺顺手的。
turns.belief_state: 自我效能感在特定情境下仍有微弱留存

sessions.ending_state: 出现了一次轻微的观念碰撞与防御，但在引导下客户自发觉察到了一丝并非全然无能的证据，为下一步行为激活埋下伏笔。

sessions.goal: 设计行为实验，打破社交退缩与抑郁情绪的恶性循环

turns.speaker: therapist
turns.text: 萨莉，上周你提到帮高中朋友梳理论文大纲时感觉还不错，回想这件事，你现在有什么新的感受吗？
turns.belief_state: 利用客户自身的积极经验作为干预支点

turns.speaker: client
turns.text: 当时觉得挺自然的，但事后又觉得那只是帮个小忙，算不了什么。我还是觉得面对陌生人或者班里的同学，我做不到。
turns.belief_state: 习惯性贬低自己的积极成就

turns.speaker: therapist
turns.text: 你看，我们的大脑很擅长把积极的体验‘抹去’，只留下消极的部分。今天我想邀请你做一个小小的行为实验，不是让你马上去参加盛大派对，而是在这周里，尝试一件非常微小、可控的事情。
turns.belief_state: 微型行为实验比宏大目标更容易被抑郁客户接受

turns.speaker: client
turns.text: 多小的事？如果又是去上课或者跟人聊天，我大概率会临阵脱逃。
turns.belief_state: 害怕再次面对失败带来的挫败感

turns.speaker: therapist
turns.text: 比如，这周去食堂买早餐时，试着对收银员说一声‘谢谢，祝你今天愉快’，然后观察对方的反应，以及你脑子里出现什么想法。你觉得这个难度怎么样？
turns.belief_state: 通过极低门槛的实验来挑战社交焦虑认知

turns.speaker: client
turns.text: 只是说句话？这听起来……好像没那么吓人。但我还是有点担心他们会觉得我很奇怪。
turns.belief_state: 他人对我的负面评价是不可避免的

turns.speaker: therapist
turns.text: 担心被觉得奇怪是很正常的预测。我们可以把这个担忧当成一个假设：‘如果我说谢谢，他们一定会觉得我很奇怪’。这只是一个假设，不是事实。这周我们去检验它，好吗？
turns.belief_state: 将预测转化为待检验的科学假设

turns.speaker: client
turns.text: 好吧，听上去像是个科学实验。我愿意试试看，反正风险很低。如果搞砸了，大不了也就这样了。
turns.belief_state: 愿意承担微小风险去检验自动化思维

sessions.ending_state: 客户接受了低门槛的行为实验方案，咨询关系进一步加深，展现出初步的行动意愿和灵活度。
